Why every decor project starts with arithmetic

The most common question we get before a purchase isn't about colour or price. It's "how much do I need?" And getting it wrong costs twice over: order too little and the second order may come from a different batch with a slightly different shade; order far too much and you have money sitting in boxes that will never be opened.

The calculation itself is simple. A tape measure and a sheet of paper will do it.

How to calculate each type

Flooring: parquet and carpet

Work out the floor area: length × width in metres. If the room is irregular, split it into rectangles and add the areas together. Then add a waste allowance, and check the product page for the coverage per box in square metres — we publish it in the specifications of every product — and divide your total area by it to get the number of boxes.

Walls: wallpaper and cladding

Work out each wall: width × height, then add up the walls you're covering. Subtract doors and large windows only; leave small openings in the calculation as a safety margin. Then check the roll or panel coverage on the product page.

Skirting boards and trims

Skirting is measured by length, not area: add up the room's perimeter and subtract the width of the doorways.

Quick comparison table

ProductMeasured inFormulaWatch out for
ParquetSquare metresLength × widthBox coverage varies between products
WallpaperSquare metresWidth × height per wallLarge repeats need more waste for matching
Wall claddingSquare metresWidth × heightSubtract doors and large windows only
SkirtingLinear metresPerimeter − doorway widthsCorners need extra pieces
Marble alternativeSquare metresWidth × heightPanel size determines the joint layout

The five most common mistakes

  • Measuring from the furniture instead of wall to wall.
  • Assuming the room is a perfect rectangle — measure length and width in at least two places.
  • Allowing no waste at all, then having to order one extra box from a different colour batch.
  • Subtracting every small opening until the quantity falls short.
  • Working from the architect's drawing instead of measuring the finished room.

A worked example: a 4 × 5 metre room

Take a bedroom 5 metres long, 4 metres wide and 3 metres high, with one door and one window.

The floor: 5 × 4 = 20 m². Open the product page for whatever you've chosen — say Chinese herringbone parquet in warm grey, 8 mm — read the coverage per box from the specifications, and divide 20 by it after adding your waste allowance.

One feature wall: if the wall behind the bed is 4 metres wide and 3 metres high, that's 12 m². Choose your wallpaper against that figure — for example Korean plain wallpaper in light pink or Korean grey marble-effect wallpaper.

Skirting: perimeter = (5 + 4) × 2 = 18 linear metres, minus the width of the doorway.

Three formulas, two minutes with a calculator.

Why choose Texa Decor?

We offer a measuring service before purchase — our team comes out, measures, and specifies the exact quantity, which removes the problem at its source. Browse parquet, wallpaper or wall cladding, then contact us to book a visit.

Frequently asked questions

How much waste allowance should I add?

It varies with the laying pattern, the room shape and the size of the repeat. Straight laying in a regular room needs the least; herringbone or a large pattern repeat needs more. Contact us after measuring and we'll work out the right allowance for your project.

Where do I find the coverage per box or roll?

On the product page itself, in the specifications section, alongside the thickness, material and country of origin.

Should I order the whole quantity at once?

Yes, and strongly so. Ordering in two goes can mean a slight shade difference between batches, and that difference is obvious once everything is installed.

One last tip

Keep one full box back after installation. Floors and cladding get scratched or chipped over time, and having pieces from the same batch means an invisible repair rather than a patch in a slightly different shade.
